questions.stem: How do you estimate the gradient of a curve at a particular point?

options.text: Draw a tangent to the curve at that point and find its gradient
Calculate the gradient between the first and last points on the curve
Measure the area under the curve

questions.explanation: A tangent is a straight line that just touches the curve at a single point. Finding the gradient of this tangent gives an estimate of the gradient of the curve at that point.

questions.stem: At a turning point (maximum or minimum) of a curve, what is the gradient?
questions.explanation: At a turning point, the curve changes direction. The tangent at this point is horizontal, so its gradient is 0.

questions.stem: A tangent is drawn to a curve at a point. The tangent passes through $(1, 3)$ and $(5, 11)$. What is the gradient of the curve at that point?
questions.explanation: The gradient of the tangent is $\frac{11 - 3}{5 - 1} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$. The gradient of the curve at the point of tangency equals the gradient of the tangent.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph that is curved, what does the gradient of the tangent at a point represent?

options.text: The instantaneous speed at that moment

questions.explanation: On a distance-time graph, the gradient gives the speed. When the graph is curved, the tangent at a point gives the instantaneous speed at that particular moment.

questions.stem: If a curve is decreasing (going downward from left to right) at a point, what can you say about the gradient there?
questions.explanation: When a curve is decreasing, the $y$-values are getting smaller as $x$ increases. The tangent slopes downward, giving a negative gradient.

questions.stem: Why does the gradient of a curve change from point to point, unlike a straight line?

options.text: Because curves have more than one $y$-intercept
Because the steepness and direction of the curve vary at different positions
Because curves do not have a gradient

questions.explanation: A straight line has constant steepness, but a curve bends. At each point, the tangent has a different slope, so the gradient changes continuously along the curve.

questions.stem: A tangent to the curve $y = x^2$ at $x = 3$ passes through $(3, 9)$ and $(4, 15)$. What is the estimated gradient at $x = 3$?
questions.explanation: Gradient of tangent $= \frac{15 - 9}{4 - 3} = \frac{6}{1} = 6$. This matches the actual derivative of $x^2$ at $x = 3$, which is $2x = 6$.
